ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of directors, shareholders, beneficial owners, and material maritime counterparties against OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Sanctions Consolidated List, Canada's listed persons under the Special Economic Measures Act and UN Act, EU consolidated sanctions lists, and proprietary PEP databases. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, family member, or close associate under FINTRAC guidance. Screening must be repeated at incorporation and on any material ownership change; results must be documented and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Corporate Access online service; accessible through alberta.ca/corporate-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in English or French; all names must be available in Latin characters for the NUANS search. The correct legal element for an unlimited liability company is 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC' as a suffix. Names in non-Latin scripts are transliterated for the NUANS report but the registered name retains the approved Latin-script form. Consonant clusters, spaces, capitalization, and punctuation are subject to Alberta corporate naming conventions.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 business days of receiving a ministerial refusal, submit a written reconsideration request to the Director of Registries at Service Alberta, including a corrected NUANS report, the corporation's name rationale, and supporting professional letters. If the Director upholds the refusal, an appeal may be filed with the Alberta Court of King's Bench pursuant to Alberta Rules of Court, requesting review of the registration decision. A clarified or alternate name may be filed immediately while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible for an Alberta ULC only when the provider maintains a physical street address in Alberta at which a natural person is available during normal business hours and at which statutory books and records may be inspected. A bare post office box or mail-forwarding address is not acceptable. For a maritime towage and salvage operation, use of a virtual office is allowed in the pre-incorporation phase but a registered physical logistics address may be expected by Transport Canada and the Canada Revenue Agency for commercial substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5–8% annually) for a conventional Alberta registered office. The risk may increase to 15% if the virtual office provider is shared with high-risk clientele; Transport Canada vessel safety and marine fisheries inspections are administered against the operator rather than the registered office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 5-17 (incorporation), s 5(1) (ULC election), s 101 (registered office), s 102 (records office), s 119 (share capital and liability rules)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Service Alberta — Corporate Registry Division (Alberta Business Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Articles of Incorporation under the ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA for ULCs. Share subscription proceeds may be held in a corporate escrow or operating bank account; adequate paid-in capital is recommended solely to satisfy marine insurer underwriting requirements, and all subscription proceeds must be deposited before share certificates are issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED that the directors approve and accept the share subscription agreements for the issued common shares and direct the corporate secretary to issue the corresponding share certificates. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED that the registered office be fixed at Suite 300, 4900 5th Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, Canada T2M 2H5 and the statutory minute book maintained there. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED that Captain [NAME], Mr./Ms. [NAME] and [NAME] be appointed respectively as Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Salvage and Safety Officer, with authority to open bank accounts, execute towage and salvage contracts, and file maritime regulatory applications. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED that the officers obtain all environmental, fire safety and occupational clearances before operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search, Reservation and ULC Name Suffix Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized NUANS broker or Alberta Business Registry online name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search and reserve the proposed corporate name for 90 days. The name must end with 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or the abbreviation 'ULC'. Incorporate the approved name into the draft Form 1 and attach the NUANS report.
required_dossiers: Third-party consent to use a name (if applicable)
Draft Articles of Incorporation containing the reserved name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on distinctiveness or public-interest grounds, request reconsideration from the Registrar or file a new NUANS search within the 90-day reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation (Form 1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 under ABCA s 6, designating the corporation as an unlimited liability corporation. Set the authorized share capital (no-par common shares), designate the registered office and first directors, and execute the form with the required declarations. Where a director resides outside Alberta, attach the personal information consent and proof of identity.
required_dossiers: First directors' consent and identity proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, cure formal defects under ABCA s 14 (correction of articles) or apply for a Director's order under s 280; the filer has 30 days to cure before rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing, Statutory Fee Payment and Certificate of Incorporation Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service Alberta — Alberta Business Registry (corporate online services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Form 1 electronically through an authorized service provider or the Alberta Business Registry portal, pay the C$100 corporate applications fee, and await issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. The ULC comes into existence on the certificate date.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic filing is rejected, correct the deficiency within 10 business days and resubmit; a disputed rejection is appealable to the Alberta Registrar under ABCA s 280.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Meeting and First Board Resolution Recordation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first directors' meeting or execute unanimous written resolutions, formally adopting the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office location and officer appointments. Record resolutions in the minute book and complete the register of directors.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defective corporate action is ratified by a subsequent directors' resolution or shareholder consent under ABCA s 8; officer appointment defects are cured by re-issuance of the appointment resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Issuance, Share Register and Shareholder Records Update
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete share subscription statements, collect subscription proceeds into the ULC operating bank account, issue share certificates carrying the statutory ULC liability notice, and update the shareholders register.
required_dossiers: Proof of subscription payment (bank statement or escrow receipt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscription is defaulted, the share issuance is reversed by substituted board resolution and the capital account is adjusted without creditor impact given the unlimited liability nature of the entity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canadian Federal/Provincial Tax Registration and Municipal Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Alberta Corporate Registry, municipality of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, register the ULC with CRA for corporate income tax (RR0001), GST/HST (RT0001), and payroll (RP0001) where applicable. Confirm provincial corporate tax filing is integrated through the CRA corporate assessment. Submit municipal business licence application for the registered office/shore-side premises.
required_dossiers: CRA business number application (Form RC159 or online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is refused for identity mismatch, correct the Business Number profile in CRA My Business Account and resubmit; municipal licence denials are appealable to the local business licence appeal tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada Marine Safety Directorate; Alberta Safety Codes Council; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Transport Canada Vessel Registry Certificate and Marine Safety Management System Operating Permit; AEPA Industrial Approval for shoreside salvage/workshop activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) in coordination with Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EPEA Category B Registration / Screening for vessel maintenance and fuel storage; full EIA (Category A) required where significant adverse effects on fish-bearing waters are anticipated under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-38, Sch. A
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero oil discharge per Fisheries Act s.36(3); 15 ppm oily-water separator limits for machinery bilge water; Alberta Air Quality Objectives (A.R. 100/2007) for VOC and particulate emissions; ballast water treatment meeting Canadian Ballast Water Regulations thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code safety certification (Division B hazardous occupancy) for onshore salvage yards and fuel storage areas; structural load inspections and underground utility permits issued by the Alberta Safety Codes Council; Alberta OHS pre-work clearance and fall protection registration for elevated barge and mooring areas; federal fire safety plan under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 for crew accommodation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes and Alberta Treasury Board and Finance for provincial taxes; official portals at canada.ca/revenue-agency and alberta.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Canadian entities obtain a Business Number (BN) by registering online through the CRA's My Business Account portal; foreign entities must register for GST/HST if carrying on business in Canada exceeding the registration threshold
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; ULCs are automatically treated as pass-through entities for Canadian income tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and transfer pricing provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 economic turnover threshold triggering mandatory GST registration
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: GST/HST returns must be filed electronically via CRA's My Business Account; no mandatory real-time digital stamping for all transactions but digital reporting requirements are being phased in for certain large taxpayers; electronic invoices recommended for compliance

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada qualify for 0% GST rate if not consumed in Canada. Offshore services such as maritime towage and salvage performed outside Canada are zero-rated if the service is not performed in Canada and consideration is paid to a non-resident or meets specific conditions under the Excise Tax Act.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA conducts audits on export claims; penalties for fraudulent zero-rating claims include fines up to 200% of the tax evaded and potential criminal prosecution; retrospective clawback of zero-rated GST if documentation is deemed insufficient

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC). No standalone foreign exchange administration body is designated; the Minister of Finance retains residual statutory authority over currency and investment policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar has full current-account and capital-account convertibility under the Currency Act, Bank of Canada Act, and the common-law framework. There are no exchange controls, licensing requirements, or quantitative limits on conversion or repatriation. Profit remittance from an Alberta ULC is lawful through dividends, shareholder loan repayments, or deemed distributions, but Canada imposes Part XIII non-resident withholding tax at a 25% statutory rate (often reduced by treaty), and an unlimited liability corporation requires careful tax characterization because of its pass-through and deemed-dividend rules. Offshore towage and salvage revenue can be paid into a Canadian account without currency surrender, but foreign-currency balances must be reported in Canadian-dollar equivalent under the Income Tax Act and IFRS functional-currency rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Cross-border towage and salvage export receipts may be retained in any foreign currency. Where receipts enter a Canadian bank account, FINTRAC reporting obligations apply to cross-border electronic funds transfers and large-cash/EFT transactions of C$10,000 or more. For tax purposes, all foreign-currency receipts and exchange gains/losses must be translated into the ULC's functional currency in accordance with subsection 261(3) of the Income Tax Act, with a documented audit trail maintained for the T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; no time window or conversion ratio is imposed.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for payment-orchestration and information rails; Low as the sole primary depository or escrow bank. An offshore electronic-money institution is not a bank under the Bank Act and cannot accept deposits or perform banking business in Canada; it must rely on a Canadian Schedule I bank for deposit-holding. A foreign fintech can be engaged as a money service business registered with FINTRAC and, once the transitional regime is phased in, as a payment service provider under the Retail Payment Activities Act administered by the Bank of Canada. For an Alberta ULC in deep-sea towage and salvage, the compliant treasury structure is a Schedule I bank account as the protected escrow/operational account, with the fintech used only for payment routing, FX quotation, and reconciliation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: FINTRAC client-identification rules permit remote verification where the bank uses reliable dual-process technology or a credible source plus corroborating identification, so a purely remote opening is legally possible. In practice, Canadian banks will require at least one natural person who is a director, practical controller, or authorized signatory to complete a live interview—physical at a Canadian branch, or video interview where the bank's risk appetite allows. For enhanced-risk maritime towage/salvage and offshore beneficial owners, physical attendance at an Alberta branch or before a Canadian notary/consular officer is strongly advised to prevent onboarding delays. The ULC must present passport and proof of address for each authorized signatory, corporate authorization and incumbency certificates, a current Alberta registry certificate, and a complete source-of-funds narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear beneficial ownership around the Unlimited Liability Company and foreign parent group
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an equity-chain schedule, share ledger and shareholder register, Alberta Corporate Registry navigation search, organizational chart, articles/memorandum of the ULC, unanimous shareholder agreement, passport copies of all direct and indirect owners, and a Canadian legal opinion confirming the ULC's ownership, unlimited liability nature, and tax classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk maritime trade activity (deep-sea towage, salvage, offshore emergency response) with unfamiliar counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the operational dossier comprising BIMCO or Lloyd's Standard Form towage/salvage contracts, P&I Club and hull/machinery insurance certificates, flag-state registration, ISM/ISPS compliance certificates, Transport Canada licences under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, an intended-account-usage letter, and a list of charterers, brokers, and offshore agents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound wires for capital injection or Lloyd's salvage award proceeds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Retain an evidence bundle with executed share subscription or escrow agreement, source-of-funds statements from the ultimate remitter's regulated bank, underlying invoice or salvage award/arbitral order, beneficiary-bank reference, and a contemporaneous treasury instruction letter from a ULC director or CFO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding and non-resident director with no Canadian banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver certified passport and secondary identity document, notarized certificate of incumbency, proof of residential address from a durable source, attestation letters from a home-jurisdiction regulated bank, a two-step remote-verification record, and availability for live video interview and follow-up CDD.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/negative-media screening overlaps due to vessel flag, parent-country exposure, or marine-sub-sector screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a sanctions-clearance analysis of all owners, vessels, charterers, and salvage counterparties against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions, OFAC, UN, and UK sanctions lists; include IMO vessel numbers and Lloyd's registry extracts; offer a negative-news covenant and a waiver permitting ongoing transactional screening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer from the non-resident parent/investor to the ULC's capital-escrow account at a Canadian Schedule I bank, with the beneficiary name exactly matching the Alberta ULC registered legal name. Insert ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI for share capital or INTC for intra-company funding; in field 70 use the narrative 'Alberta ULC capital subscription / shareholder loan – ISIC 5222 offshore towage and salvage'. Accompany the wire with a share subscription agreement or shareholder loan agreement, director resolution, source-of-funds confirmation from the remitting bank, and, if structured as escrowed capital, a Canadian legal opinion. Investment Canada Act notification is triggered only if a non-Canadian acquires control of a Canadian business above statutory monetary thresholds, including an acquisition by a foreign parent of the ULC; a filing calendar should be prepared.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for bunkers, crew wages, port dues, insurance, salvage subcontracts, and emergency-response costs should be settled using: (i) domestic Canadian-dollar clearing via Payments Canada Lynx and ACSS; (ii) cross-border USD/CAD/EUR wires via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code TRAD and a narrative identifying the relevant Lloyd's Open Form or BIMCO contract; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit opened through a Canadian Schedule I bank under UCP600 using SWIFT MT700/MT707/MT798; and (iv) a designated escrow account for Lloyd's salvage-reward settlements, released only upon a salvage award, interim payment certificate, or agreed escrow instruction. The ULC must maintain a clearing-rail matrix listing beneficiary bank BICs, account numbers, intermediary banks, sanctions pre-screening, and FINTRAC EFT-reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign-exchange contracts for immediate CAD/USD/EUR funding
Outright FX forwards and rollover forwards executed with Canadian Schedule I banks or OSFI-regulated derivatives dealers
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for minor or illiquid currencies encountered in offshore salvage jurisdictions
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for vessel-financing and debt-service exposure
Simple FX options used to hedge committed salvage and towage revenue cash flows
Zero-cost FX collar strategies for protecting Canadian-dollar profit margins

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Corporation Annual Return (Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c.B-9, s.265)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary date of incorporation (i.e., incorporation anniversary plus 60 calendar days)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No immediate late fee; after 3 consecutive default years the Registrar may administratively dissolve the ULC; reinstatement requires payment of arrears, late fees, and formal reinstatement application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c.1 (5th Supp.), s.150)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six calendar months after the taxation year-end (e.g., December 31 fiscal year-end is due by June 30 the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under ITA s.162(1) of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month, up to 12 months; repeated penalties at 10% plus 2% per month; daily interest applies on balances; directors may face personal liability for certain unremitted amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory asset, revenue, or employee threshold triggers independent audit under Alberta's Business Corporations Act; an auditor must be appointed unless all shareholders unanimously waive the appointment by written resolution. For offshore towage and salvage ULCs, contractual lenders or charter parties may independently require an audited financial statement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or ASPE as issued by the Accounting Standards Board (AcSB) are permitted; ASPE is standard for private ULCs; IFRS is mandatory only for publicly accountable enterprises or if shareholders elect IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Alberta's Business Corporations Act Part 20.1, the ULC must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register and update it within 15 days of any share transfer or change in significant control. The annual return contains a declaration confirming compliance with ISC recordkeeping; Alberta does not require filing the ISC register separately with the Corporate Registry.

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
